rows.longest_span: define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals or both and societies that can result from the development provision or use of ai systems the assessment shall determine the potential consequences
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.4 requires the organization to define a process for assessing the potential consequences for individuals or groups of individuals, or both, and societies, that can result from the development, provision or use of AI systems. The assessment shall determine the potential consequences of the system's deployment, intended use and foreseeable misuse; shall take into account the specific technical and societal context and applicable jurisdictions; and its result shall be documented. The organization shall consider the results in the risk assessment referred to in 6.1.2.

rows.longest_span: can be subject to some degree of verification should be accepted as audit evidence where the degree of verification is low the auditor should use professional judgement to determine
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.4.7 states that information relevant to the audit objectives, scope and criteria should be collected by appropriate sampling and should be verified as far as practicable, and that only information which can be subject to some degree of verification should be accepted as audit evidence. Where the degree of verification is low, the auditor should use professional judgement to determine how much reliance to place on it. Evidence leading to findings should be recorded.

rows.longest_span: auditors should be independent of the activity being audited wherever practicable and should in all cases act in a manner free from bias and conflict of interest
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.6 states that auditors should be independent of the activity being audited wherever practicable, and should in all cases act in a manner free from bias and conflict of interest. It adds that when it is not possible for internal auditors to be independent of the activity being audited, every effort should be made to remove bias and encourage objectivity. The principle is therefore conditional by its own wording, and neither ISO 19011 nor ISO/IEC 42001 forbids auditing work one has contributed to.

rows.longest_span: it is not possible for internal auditors to be independent of the activity being audited every effort should be made to remove bias and encourage objectivity
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.6 states that where it is not possible for internal auditors to be independent of the activity being audited, every effort should be made to remove bias and encourage objectivity. Neither ISO 19011 nor ISO/IEC 27001 contains a rule that an auditor may not audit their own work - that formulation is practice convention.

rows.longest_span: plan implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and to implement the actions determined in clause 6 by establishing criteria for the processes
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 8.1 requires the organization to plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and to implement the actions determined in Clause 6, by establishing criteria for the processes and implementing control in accordance with those criteria. It further requires the organization to implement the controls determined according to 6.1.3 that relate to the operation of the AIMS, and requires that the effectiveness of those controls be monitored and corrective actions considered where intended results are not achieved.

rows.longest_span: when the organization determines the need for changes to the ai management system the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.3 requires that when the organization determines the need for changes to the AI management system, the changes shall be carried out in a planned manner. Clause 8.1 adds control of planned changes and review of the consequences of unintended ones. A change to an AI system's purpose, data or deployment context is where role determination and impact assessment can both fall out of date.

rows.longest_span: an important means of collecting information carried out in a manner adapted to the situation and the individual face to face or
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 Annex A.17 treats interviews as an important means of collecting information, carried out in a manner adapted to the situation and the individual, face-to-face or by other means. It asks that interviews be held with individuals from appropriate levels and functions performing activities within the audit scope, normally during working hours and where practical at the normal workplace, that the interviewee be put at ease, and that the reason for the interview and any note taking be explained.

rows.longest_span: that the ai policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability adequacy and effectiveness
rows.description: Table A.1 control A.2.4 states that the AI policy shall be reviewed at planned intervals or additionally as needed to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness. Like every Table A.1 control it applies where the organization has selected it under clause 6.1.3 and declared it in the statement of applicability. Clause 5.2 requires the policy to exist; A.2.4 is where periodic review of it comes from.

rows.longest_span: arrangements for a set of one or more audits planned for a specific time frame and directed towards a specific purpose
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.5 defines it as arrangements for a set of one or more audits planned for a specific time frame and directed towards a specific purpose.

rows.longest_span: establish an ai policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization provides a framework for setting ai objectives
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 5.2 requires top management to establish an AI policy that is appropriate to the purpose of the organization, provides a framework for setting AI objectives, and includes commitments to meet applicable requirements and to continual improvement. The policy shall be available as documented information, refer as relevant to other organizational policies, be communicated within the organization, and be available to interested parties as appropriate. This is a clause requirement and applies whether or not control A.2.2 is selected.

rows.longest_span: the audit client should ensure audit programme objectives are established to direct the planning and conducting of audits and
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 5.2 states that the audit client should ensure audit programme objectives are established to direct the planning and conducting of audits, and that those objectives should be consistent with the audit client's strategic direction and context and support its management system policies and objectives. The clause lists what they can be based on, including the needs and expectations of interested parties, management system requirements, the auditee's level of performance, and the need to evaluate organizations in the supply chain.

rows.longest_span: should substantively influence the planning and implementation of the audit programme and the planning conducting and reporting of audits
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.8 describes the risk-based approach as one that considers risks and opportunities, and states that it should substantively influence the planning and implementation of the audit programme and the planning, conducting and reporting of audits, so that audits focus on matters significant for the audit client and for achieving the programme objectives. It is expressed as a should, like every principle in clause 4, and it directs where effort concentrates rather than authorising an area to go unexamined.

rows.longest_span: organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability
rows.description: Annex B is normative because clause 6.1.3 e) requires the organization to consider the guidance in Annex B for the implementation of the controls it has determined. What binds is the act of considering, not the content of any particular sentence. Clause B.1 makes the limit explicit: organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability, and the guidance is not always suitable or sufficient in all situations.

rows.longest_span: organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability
rows.description: Annex B of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 is normative but its content is written as should, and clause B.1 states that organizations do not have to document or justify inclusion or exclusion of implementation guidance in the statement of applicability, and that the guidance is not always suitable or sufficient in all situations. A nonconformity therefore cannot be raised because an organization implemented a control differently from the Annex B guidance. What clause 6.1.3 e) requires is that the guidance be considered.

rows.longest_span: where an organization performs work or provides a service using an online environment enabling individuals to execute processes
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 describes a virtual location as one where an organization performs work or provides a service using an online environment, enabling individuals to execute processes irrespective of physical location. Much of an AI management system's evidence lives in exactly such places: model registries, pipelines, cloud environments and logging platforms. Clause 3.6 notes that audit scope generally includes a description of virtual as well as physical locations.

rows.longest_span: define and establish an ai risk assessment process that is informed by and aligned with the ai policy
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.2 requires the organization to define and establish an AI risk assessment process that is informed by and aligned with the AI policy and AI objectives, is designed so that repeated assessments produce consistent, valid and comparable results, identifies risks that aid or prevent achieving the AI objectives, analyses those risks, and evaluates them. The requirement is on the process and its properties.

rows.longest_span: not all the control objectives and controls listed in table a 1 are required to be used and
rows.description: Annex A.1 of ISO/IEC 42001:2023 states that not all the control objectives and controls listed in Table A.1 are required to be used, and that the organization can design and implement its own controls. A Table A.1 shall therefore operates conditionally: it applies to the organization that has determined the control necessary and declared it. Writing that ISO/IEC 42001 requires an AI policy control misstates this; writing that where A.2.2 is selected the organization shall document an AI policy does not.

rows.longest_span: include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the ai management system and
rows.description: Clause 9.3.3 requires the results of the management review to include decisions related to continual improvement opportunities and any need for changes to the AI management system, and requires documented information to be available as evidence of those results. A review that records attendance and discussion but no decisions has not produced what 9.3.3 asks for.

rows.longest_span: understand the appropriateness and consequences of using information and communications technology tools and emerging technology to conduct audits
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 7.2.3 item 10 requires auditors to understand the appropriateness and consequences of using information and communications technology tools, and emerging technology, to conduct audits. The requirement is general: it covers remote-audit tooling, sampling and analysis software, and whatever arrives next.

rows.longest_span: auditors should be independent of the activity being audited wherever practicable and should in all cases act
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.6 states auditors should be independent of the activity being audited wherever practicable, and should in all cases act free from bias and conflict of interest.

rows.longest_span: determine external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect its ability to achieve the intended
rows.description: Clause 4.1 requires the organization to determine external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect its ability to achieve the intended outcomes of its ISMS.

rows.longest_span: evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled note
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.1 defines an audit as a systematic, independent and documented process for obtaining objective evidence and evaluating it objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled. Note 2 to entry adds that an internal audit is conducted by, or on behalf of, the organization itself. An organization may therefore engage a contracted auditor and the audit remains a first-party audit; what makes it internal is whose management system is being examined, not who holds the pen.

rows.longest_span: in clauses 5 to 7 is based on the seven outlined in 4 2 to 4 8
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 presents the seven principles without ranking them. Clause 4.1 says only that adherence to them is fundamental and that the guidance in Clauses 5 to 7 is based on the seven outlined in 4.2 to 4.8. It says nothing about precedence in either direction; the words precedence, hierarchy and rank do not appear in the document. Where two principles engage a situation differently, nothing in the text decides between them and the auditor weighs them. The absence of a ranking rule is an observation about the text, not a stated rule of no ranking.

rows.longest_span: each individual audit should be based on defined audit objectives scope and criteria consistent with the overall
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 5.5.2 states that each individual audit should be based on defined audit objectives, scope and criteria, consistent with the overall programme objectives. It lists what the objectives can include: determining the extent of conformity to the criteria, evaluating the management system's capability to meet statutory, regulatory and other requirements, evaluating its effectiveness in meeting intended results, and finding opportunities for improvement.

rows.longest_span: determine external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect its ability to achieve the intended
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 4.1 requires the organization to determine external and internal issues relevant to its purpose that affect its ability to achieve the intended results of its AI management system, to consider the intended purpose of the AI systems it develops, provides or uses, and to determine its roles with respect to those systems. It also requires the organization to determine whether climate change is a relevant issue. All four are stated as shall.

rows.longest_span: as part of resource identification the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences
rows.description: Table A.1 control A.4.6 states that, as part of resource identification, the organization shall document information about the human resources and their competences used across the AI system life cycle, covering development, deployment, operation, change management, maintenance and transfer. Where selected, it produces a record that can be read against the competence determined under clause 7.2.

rows.longest_span: implement any action needed review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken and make changes to the
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 10.2 requires that when a nonconformity occurs the organization shall react to it, taking action to control and correct it and dealing with the consequences as applicable; evaluate the need for action to eliminate the causes so it does not recur or occur elsewhere, by reviewing the nonconformity, determining its causes and determining whether similar nonconformities exist or could occur; implement any action needed; review the effectiveness of any corrective action taken; and make changes to the AIMS if necessary. Corrective actions shall be appropriate to the effects of the nonconformities encountered.

rows.longest_span: review the organization's ai management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability adequacy and effectiveness
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 9.3.1 requires top management to review the organization's AI management system at planned intervals to ensure its continuing suitability, adequacy and effectiveness. Clause 9.3.2 lists the required inputs and 9.3.3 the required outputs. Documented information shall be available as evidence of the results of management reviews.

rows.longest_span: the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 9.2.2 states that the organization shall plan, establish, implement and maintain an audit programme including frequency, methods, responsibilities, planning requirements and reporting; that when establishing it the organization shall consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits; and that the organization shall define the audit objectives, criteria and scope for each audit, select auditors and conduct audits so as to ensure objectivity and impartiality, and ensure results are reported to relevant managers. Documented information shall be available as evidence of the programme's implementation and of the audit results.

rows.longest_span: obtain and evaluate evidence about some characteristic of that population in order to form a conclusion
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 Annex A.6.1 describes sampling as what takes place when it is not practical or cost-effective to examine all available information, and defines it as selecting less than one hundred per cent of the population to obtain and evaluate evidence about some characteristic of that population in order to form a conclusion about it. It states the associated risk plainly: the sample is not necessarily representative, so the auditor's conclusion can differ from the one the whole population would have produced.

rows.longest_span: the organization shall consider the results of the ai system impact assessment in the risk assessment
rows.description: Clause 6.1.4 states that the organization shall consider the results of the AI system impact assessment in the risk assessment. The requirement is directional and it is a shall. Evidence that satisfies it shows the impact findings appearing in the risk assessment record; an impact assessment filed separately and never referenced leaves this requirement unevidenced even where both documents exist and are individually sound.

rows.longest_span: ensure that externally provided processes products or services relevant to the ai management system are controlled
rows.description: Clause 8.1 requires the organization to control planned changes and review the consequences of unintended changes, and to ensure that externally provided processes, products or services relevant to the AI management system are controlled. For an AI management system this reaches third-party models, datasets and hosted services, which is where Table A.1 family A.10 on third-party and customer relationships becomes relevant if selected.

rows.longest_span: the risk based approach should substantively influence the planning and implementation of the audit programme
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.8 states the risk-based approach should substantively influence the planning and implementation of the audit programme, so that audits focus on matters significant to the audit client and to the programme objectives.

rows.longest_span: select auditors and conduct audits that ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process
rows.description: Requires the organization to select auditors and conduct audits that ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process. This sentence is the whole of what ISO/IEC 27001 states on auditor independence.

rows.longest_span: for conducting audit activities from any place other than the location of the auditee the
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.4 defines it as a method for conducting audit activities from any place other than the location of the auditee. The definition is sourced from ISO/IEC TS 17012:2024, whose guidance the 2026 edition imports.

rows.longest_span: records statements of fact or other information which are relevant to the audit criteria and
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.10 defines audit evidence as records, statements of fact or other information which are relevant to the audit criteria and verifiable.

rows.longest_span: data security and management confidentiality and the need for contingency plans due to technology failure
rows.description: Annex A.16 names data security and management, confidentiality, and the need for contingency plans due to technology failure among the considerations remote auditing methods introduce.

rows.longest_span: select auditors and conduct audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 9.2.2 b) states that the organization shall select auditors and conduct audits to ensure objectivity and the impartiality of the audit process. That is the whole of the standard's requirement on the point: it names no independence rule, no separation of duties and no prohibition on auditing one's own area. The detail of how objectivity is achieved is left to the organization, and ISO 19011 clause 4.6 is where the guidance sits.

rows.longest_span: the rational method for reaching reliable and reproducible audit conclusions in a systematic audit process
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.7 describes the evidence-based approach as the rational method for reaching reliable and reproducible audit conclusions in a systematic audit process. It states that audit evidence should be verifiable and should be based on samples of the information available, since an audit runs for a specified duration with finite resources, and that appropriate sampling should be applied because this bears directly on the confidence that can be placed in the conclusions.

rows.longest_span: an audit using remote methods uses technology during the audit process for observing interviewing and
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 Annex A.16 records that an audit using remote methods uses technology during the audit process for observing, interviewing and verifying objective evidence, and that remote methods can introduce additional risks and opportunities. The verification test in Annex A.5 does not change with the method: the auditor still asks whether the information is complete, correct, consistent and current, and whether its integrity can be assessed.

rows.longest_span: using remote auditing methods can introduce additional risks and opportunities to the audit process
rows.description: Annex A.16 states that using remote auditing methods can introduce additional risks and opportunities to the audit process, naming data security, confidentiality and contingency planning for technology failure among the considerations.

rows.longest_span: is closely related to the confidence that can be placed in the audit conclusions
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.7 states audit evidence should be based on samples because an audit runs for a specified duration with finite resources, and that appropriate use of sampling is closely related to the confidence that can be placed in the audit conclusions.

rows.longest_span: documented information shall be available as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 5.5.7 addresses managing audit related records. ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 9.2.2 separately requires that documented information shall be available as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme and of the audit results. The standard's requirement is the one a nonconformity can be raised against; the ISO 19011 guidance describes what good record management looks like.

rows.longest_span: designed such that repeated ai risk assessments can produce consistent valid and comparable results
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 6.1.2 b) requires the process to be designed such that repeated AI risk assessments can produce consistent, valid and comparable results. This is testable: two assessments of similar systems, performed by different people, that reach materially different conclusions on the same facts indicate a process that does not meet 6.1.2 b), and the evidence for the finding is the organization's own assessment records.

rows.longest_span: nonconformities can be graded depending on the context of the organization and its risks
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001 uses only the term nonconformity and defines no severity scheme. A major and minor distinction comes from third-party certification practice under ISO/IEC 17021-1. ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.4.8 records that nonconformities can be graded depending on the context of the organization and its risks, that grading can be quantitative or qualitative, and that where grading is used the criteria should be defined and communicated by the auditing organization. Unlike ISO/IEC 27001, which relies on ISO/IEC 27000 for the term, ISO/IEC 42001 defines nonconformity itself at clause 3.16 as non-fulfilment of a requirement, alongside conformity at 3.15 and corrective action at 3.17.

rows.longest_span: declaration of nonconformity including a description explaining why the audit criteria are not fulfilled
rows.description: The link is what a finding is. Evidence without a requirement is an observation; a requirement without evidence is an assertion. Annex A.18.3 c) asks for a declaration of nonconformity including a description explaining why the audit criteria are not fulfilled, which is the link stated explicitly rather than left for the reader to infer.

rows.longest_span: and unresolved diverging opinions between the audit team and the auditee should be reported
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 4.3 states that audit findings, conclusions and reports should reflect the auditing activities truthfully and accurately, that significant obstacles encountered and unresolved diverging opinions between the audit team and the auditee should be reported, and that communication should be truthful, accurate, objective, timely, clear and complete. Omitting an obstacle that weakened the audit is a failure of the principle even when every finding recorded is correct.

rows.longest_span: consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2 requires the organization, when establishing the internal audit programme, to consider the importance of the processes concerned and the results of previous audits.

rows.longest_span: professional judgement to determine the degree of reliance that can be placed on
rows.description: Where the degree of verification is low, clause 6.4.7 requires the auditor to use professional judgement to determine the degree of reliance that can be placed on the information as evidence.

rows.longest_span: implemented or not and justification for excluding any of the annex a controls
rows.description: Clause 6.1.3 d) requires the Statement of Applicability to contain the necessary controls, justification for their inclusion, whether each is implemented or not, and justification for excluding any of the Annex A controls.

rows.longest_span: carried out together at a single auditee on two or more management systems
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.2 defines a combined audit as one carried out together at a single auditee on two or more management systems.

rows.longest_span: one or more persons conducting an audit supported if needed by technical experts
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.15 defines the audit team as one or more persons conducting an audit, supported if needed by technical experts, and clause 3.17 defines a technical expert as a person who provides specific knowledge or expertise to the audit team. A technical expert supplies subject-matter understanding and does not act as an auditor. Bringing a data scientist onto the team to interpret model evaluation evidence is the intended use; having that person audit their own team's work is not.

rows.longest_span: the boundaries and applicability of the ai management system to establish its scope
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 4.3 requires the organization to determine the boundaries and applicability of the AI management system to establish its scope, considering the issues in 4.1 and the requirements in 4.2. Because 4.1 includes the determination of roles, the scope is downstream of that determination. An auditor testing scope therefore tests the role determination first: a scope that excludes an activity the organization performs in a role it holds is an exclusion that needs justification.

rows.longest_span: the individual managing the audit programme should select and determine the methods for
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 5.5.3 states that the individual managing the audit programme should select and determine the methods for conducting an audit effectively and efficiently, depending on the defined objectives, scope and criteria, and that audits can be performed on-site, remotely or as a combination, suitably balanced with consideration of associated risks and opportunities. Annex A.1 gives further guidance on applying auditing methods.

rows.longest_span: activities which can change as a result of information collected during the audit
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.3.4 covers preparing documented information for the audit, and Annex A.13 gives guidance on working documents such as checklists, sampling plans and forms for recording evidence and findings. Annex A.13 also cautions that working documents should not restrict the audit activities, which can change as a result of information collected during the audit.

rows.longest_span: the boundaries and applicability of the ai management system to establish its scope
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 4.3 requires the organization to determine the boundaries and applicability of the AI management system to establish its scope, considering the external and internal issues from 4.1 and the requirements of interested parties from 4.2. The scope is documented information.

rows.longest_span: are available communicating the importance of effective ai management and of conforming to
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 5.1 requires top management to demonstrate leadership and commitment by ensuring the AI policy and AI objectives are established and compatible with the strategic direction, ensuring integration of AIMS requirements into business processes, ensuring resources are available, communicating the importance of effective AI management and of conforming to AIMS requirements, ensuring the system achieves its intended results, directing and supporting persons, and promoting continual improvement. Each is auditable through artifacts rather than through attitude.

rows.longest_span: documentation of all necessary controls and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 3.26 defines the statement of applicability as documentation of all necessary controls and justification for inclusion or exclusion of controls. Clause 6.1.3 f) is the requirement that produces it. It is the document that converts the reference controls of Annex A into this organization's obligations, which is why a Table A.1 control becomes auditable only once it appears there as included.

rows.longest_span: when creating and updating documented information the organization ensure appropriate identification and description
rows.description: Clause 7.5.2 requires that when creating and updating documented information the organization ensure appropriate identification and description, format and media, and review and approval for suitability and adequacy. Clause 7.5.3 requires it to be available and suitable for use where needed, and adequately protected. Existence is not control: a current model card that nobody approved and that anyone can overwrite satisfies neither subclause.

rows.longest_span: be aware of the ai policy their contribution to the effectiveness of the
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 7.3 requires persons doing work under the organization's control to be aware of the AI policy, their contribution to the effectiveness of the AIMS, and the implications of not conforming to its requirements. Clause 7.4 requires the organization to determine the internal and external communications relevant to the AIMS, including what, when, with whom and how.

rows.longest_span: risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur
rows.description: Clause 8.2 requires the organization to perform AI risk assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur, and to retain documented information of the results. Clause 8.3 requires it to implement the AI risk treatment plan and retain documented information of the results. Where 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 require the processes to be defined, 8.2 and 8.3 require them to be run and the results kept.

rows.longest_span: declaration of nonconformity including a description explaining why the criteria are not fulfilled
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 Annex A.18.3 asks that a record of nonconformity consider a description of or reference to the audit criteria, the audit evidence, a declaration of nonconformity including a description explaining why the criteria are not fulfilled, any related findings, and the grade where grading is used. The three load-bearing parts are the criterion, the evidence, and the explanation of why the one does not meet the other.

rows.longest_span: audit findings can lead to the identification of risks opportunities for improvement or
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.11 Note 2 records that audit findings can lead to the identification of risks, opportunities for improvement, or the recording of good practices, and clause 6.4.8 provides for recording opportunities for improvement and any recommendations where the audit plan specifies. An opportunity for improvement is not a weak nonconformity: it is what an auditor records when the criteria are met and something could still be better.

rows.longest_span: subject to some degree of verification should be accepted as audit evidence
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 6.4.7 states that only information subject to some degree of verification should be accepted as audit evidence. Verification is a matter of degree, not a binary test.

rows.longest_span: assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur
rows.description: Clause 8.2 requires assessments at planned intervals or when significant changes are proposed or occur; clause 8.3 requires the treatment plan to be implemented. Both require documented information of the results.

rows.longest_span: the audit criteria are legal statutory or regulatory requirements the words compliance
rows.description: ISO 19011:2026 clause 3.8 Note 1 records that where the audit criteria are legal, statutory or regulatory requirements, the words compliance and non-compliance are often used in a finding rather than conformity language.

rows.longest_span: ensure that the results of the audits are reported to relevant management
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001 clause 9.2.2 c) requires the organization to ensure that the results of the audits are reported to relevant management.

rows.longest_span: the organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue the
rows.description: ISO/IEC 27001:2022/Amd 1:2024, Climate action changes, adds one sentence to clause 4.1: the organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue. The amendment is one page and adds nothing else to clause 4.1. It names climate change specifically, not environmental conditions.

rows.longest_span: the organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue the
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 4.1 states that the organization shall determine whether climate change is a relevant issue. The requirement is to make and record the determination; the standard does not prescribe the answer, and an organization that determines climate change is not a relevant issue and records why has met the requirement.

rows.longest_span: persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education training or experience
rows.description: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 clause 7.2 requires the organization to determine the necessary competence of persons doing work under its control that affects its AI performance, to ensure those persons are competent on the basis of appropriate education, training or experience, and where applicable to take action to acquire the necessary competence and evaluate the effectiveness of those actions. Appropriate documented information shall be available as evidence of competence.

rows.longest_span: provide a complete accurate concise and clear record of the audit and

rows.longest_span: be available as evidence of the implementation of the audit programme

rows.longest_span: to the confidence that can be placed in the audit conclusions
rows.description: Where a tool decides which records the auditor examines, it has made a sampling decision - which clause 4.7 ties directly to the confidence that can be placed in the audit conclusions.

rows.longest_span: plan implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and
rows.description: Clause 8.1 requires the organization to plan, implement and control the processes needed to meet requirements and implement the clause 6 actions, by establishing criteria and controlling the processes in accordance with them, with documented information available to have confidence the processes ran as planned.

rows.longest_span: 2 relevant interested parties can have requirements related to climate change
